Maine Crafts Association awards Yuri Kobayashi with 2026 Maine Craft Artist Award

ROCKPORT, Maine — The Maine Crafts Association has announced Yuri Kobayashi, instructor and lead fellow at The Center for Furniture Craftsmanship, as the recipient of the 2026 Maine Craft Artist Award.

This award recognizes Kobayashi's work, career, and dedication to craft education as reaching a distinguished mark of excellence. The Maine Crafts Association and the Center for Furniture Craftsmanship association welcomes all to attend the Awards Presentation and Ceremony to celebrate Kobayashi.
About The Maine Craft Artist Award

Since 2009, the Maine Crafts Association has presented this award to recognize artists whose work demonstrates distinguished excellence and whose careers have made a meaningful impact on the craft community. Award benefits include a lifetime MCA Professional membership, a $10,000 honorarium of unrestricted funds, and future teaching and exhibition opportunities with the Maine Crafts Association. The 2026 award is supported by the Maxwell/Hanrahan Foundation.
Yuri Kobayashi’s work explores the expressive possibilities of wood through a combination of traditional woodworking techniques, technical precision, and imaginative form.

Now based in Midcoast Maine, Kobayashi was born in Japan, where she earned a BA in architectural design at Musashino Art University, then trained at the Shinrin Takumi Juku, a traditional wood training school located in Takayama City, known for its long history as a woodworking region.

Following this, Kobayashi moved to the United States and received an MFA in furniture design from San Diego State University and taught for over a decade at the Rhode Island School of Design. Kobayashi has exhibited nationally and been awarded many competitive residencies, grants, and fellowships, including the Windgate Artist-in-Residencies at SUNY Purchase, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the Arizona State University Art Museum, and is a 2024 Fellow of the American Craft Council.

For the past ten years, Kobayashi has called the Center for Furniture Craftsmanship home base for her practice, as an instructor, and as Lead Fellow. Her work has made a lasting contribution to craft education through teaching, mentorship, and engagement with students learning woodworking in Maine and beyond.
